title: failure-triage-repro-checklist-prompt-lab
summary: Working scratchpad for triaging non-deterministic prompt failures and a reproducibility checklist to hand off to QA/SE teams. Focused on isolating randomness, caching, context/sliding-window effects, and template brittleness.
content:
Notes / goals:
- Purpose: create a short, repeatable repro checklist and minimal artifact set so engineers + SREs can reproduce prompting failures without chasing ephemeral state.
- Audience: prompt engineers, QA, applied-ML oncall, solutions eng.

Top-level triage flow (one-page):
1) Capture failing invocation (raw): collect model name, model_id, SDK/HTTP call, full request JSON (prompt, messages, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop tokens, streaming flag).
2) Pin runtime: exact container/image, runtime flags (use_kv_cache true/false), quantization profile.
3) Determinism step: set temperature=0, top_p=1.0, seed=42 (if runtime supports), streaming=false, and re-run. If behavior still differs, randomness likely not root cause.
4) Context isolation: truncate conversation to last N tokens (common N: 256), remove system prompt, re-run.
5) Model-variant check: compare stable -> fast -> quantized variants (e.g., v1.3.full -> v1.3.int8 -> v1.3.turbo).
6) Caching and KV effects: flush KV cache or toggle prefix_cache off. Reproduce with a cold instance.
7) Tokenization snapshot: record tokenization of the prompt and few-shot exemplars (token ids and offsets).
8) Output diffing: capture logits or token probabilities if available for first 6 tokens; otherwise capture top-5 tokens + probs.
9) Minimal prompt / few-shot: iteratively strip examples and instructions until failure disappears to find brittle fragment.
10) Regression gating: add failing case to local eval harness and create a small unit test that runs <= 10s.

Checklist (copyable):
- [ ] raw_request.json exported
- [ ] model + variant + runtime image recorded
- [ ] temperature/top_p/seed set for deterministic trial
- [ ] streaming disabled for repro run
- [ ] KV/cache toggles exercised (cold/warm)
- [ ] tokenization snapshot saved (tokens.txt)
- [ ] minimal prompt that reproduces issue (min_prompt.txt)
- [ ] small eval test added to pr (tests/prompt_regressions.py)::test_issue_xxx
- [ ] linked ticket/PR created

Common failure patterns and quick hypotheses:
- Intermittent hallucination after long context: often due to prompt truncation differences across runtime kernels (kernel may trim older tokens differently when batching). Repro: force same batch size and single-thread kernel.
- Few-shot exemplar overshadowing: when exemplar contains similar named entities that bias the model — trimming or reordering exemplars often exposes which exemplar is dominating.
- Instruction leakage between messages: check that role labels (system/user/assistant) are present and not duplicated by upstream middleware adding a system prompt.
- Tokenization boundary artifacts: punctuation attached to exemplar templates (e.g., em-dash vs hyphen) can change tokenization and change completions.
- Cache staleness: model returns older completions for repeated prefixes when prefix-KV cache not invalidated on template changes.

Minimal reproducible examples (notes):
- Failing prompt sample (redacted):
  System: You are a concise assistant that lists steps.
  User: Summarize the policy for returning equipment.
  Few-shot 1 (good): Q: How to return laptop? A: Bring serial, etc.
  Few-shot 2 (bad): Q: How to return sensitive hardware? A: Contact compliance.
  Observed issue: returns contact email verbatim with PII in ~1/20 runs.
  Hypothesis: exemplar 2 contains token sequence that triggers a retrieval-like paraphrase -> probabilistic copying.

- Minimal test to add to harness (pseudo):
  - run deterministic trial with temperature=0, streaming=false
  - assert 'email' not in response.lower()
  - if fails, reduce exemplars to 1 and re-run to identify culprit.

Diagnostics to capture (runtime artifacts):
- stdout/stderr of runtime worker for the request id
- token-level logits (if debug endpoints enabled)
- batching metadata: batch size, sequence lengths of each item
- environment variables that could affect kernel selection (e.g., RW_KERNEL_HINT)

Repro recipes (practical):
- Recipe A (quick): set temp=0; run on dedicated single-GPU instance; disable batching; disable prefix cache; capture response.
- Recipe B (deep): enable token-prob capture; run sequence-length sweep (64, 128, 256, 512) to see when failure appears; compare kernel choices in console logs.

Example minimal prompt variants to try (scratch):
- Remove system prompt entirely and prepend a short header: "Assistant: provide a numbered list."
- Replace few-shot answer text with [REDACTED] or more generic phrasing to test exemplar-specific triggers.
- Swap punctuation in exemplars (e.g., replace em-dash with comma) to test tokenization sensitivity.

Notes to self / unresolved questions:
- Can we add an internal flag to force consistent tokenization across kernels? Followup with runtime team. (See linked GH PR above.)
- Should we store token snapshots by default for slow tests or only on-demand? Cost / retention tradeoff.
- For streaming vs non-streaming divergence: need to instrument difference between partial-decoding states — file a small spike test.

Hand-off template for a reproducible bug report (one-liner + artifacts):
- one-line summary: "Intermittent PII copy in equipment-return prompt (1/20 runs)"
- artifacts: raw_request.json, min_prompt.txt, token_snapshot.json, runtime_logs.tar.gz
- reproduction steps: deterministic recipe + environment pin
- triage owner: @<owner>

To-do (short):
- [ ] convert checklist to a small wizard in Console (ask product)
- [ ] add a 'capture-token-snapshot' toggle to the debug API and default to off
- [ ] schedule a 30-min sync with serving-runtime to discuss kernel tokenization invariants

Quick references / search keywords to find related cases: "PII leak intermittent", "prompt exemplar copy", "kv cache stale prefix", "streaming vs non-streaming divergence", "tokenization boundary bug"

Last-session log (ad-hoc experiments):
- 2026-01-27: ran 50 deterministic trials with temp=0; failure rate dropped to 0/50 -> suggests randomness was a contributor.
- 2026-01-30: cold-run on dedicated instance produced failure 2/50; warm-run 6/50 -> cache seems to increase failure probability.
- 2026-02-02: reproduced consistent failure when exemplar 2 contains hyphenated serials; swapping to spaced serial removed failure.

If you're picking this up: start with the checklist, attach artifacts to the ticket, and ping me (Ethan) or Maya if you need deeper kernel logs.

-- end of scratchpad --
